Priya Nair: FYI we have another tenant whose quota/billing shows our proxy as the caller when they use partner middleware. Root cause looks like impersonation/exchange path dropping origin metadata.
Ethan K.: saw that on Monday. Their traffic is routed through partner-x which does an impersonation flow and we end up attributing to partner-x-sa.
Marco Li: quick idea: instead of HMAC headers, have proxies mint a short-lived signed JWT assertion (x-origin-assertion) that encodes {project_id, aud:gateway, iat, exp, nonce}. Proxy signs with its key and includes kid. Gateway verifies via trusted JWKS and trusts the project claim if proxy is authorized for that project.
Julia Chen: telemetry: we'll want an "assertion_status" tag (accepted|rejected|missing|invalid_kid) and keep counts per-route + per-proxy. We should also add a panel that shows attribution divergence: token_claim vs assertion_claim.
Priya Nair: sample payload (JWT claims): {"proj":"proj_123","aud":"redwood:gateway","iat":1680000000,"exp":1680000060,"nonce":"r4nd"} Header includes kid. Gateway verifies sig and aud/exp/nonce.
Ethan K.: benefits over HMAC: standard discovery (jwks), easier rotation (kid), and aud check reduces reuse. Downside: slightly larger headers.
Marco Li: pseudocode verify (go): ```go
jwt, _ := jwt.ParseWithClaims(tokStr, &Claims{}, func(t *jwt.Token) (interface{}, error) {
  kid := t.Header["kid"].(string)
  return jwks.Lookup(kid)
})
if jwt.Valid && claims.Aud == "redwood:gateway" && withinWindow(claims.Exp) && allowlist.Allows(proxyID, claims.Proj) {
  attrib = claims.Proj
  method = "assertion-jwt"
} else {
  attrib = extractFromTokenClaims(token)
  method = "token-claim"
}
emitMetric("request.attribution", map[string]string{"project": attrib, "method": method})
```
Julia Chen: dashboard: add "Attribution fidelity" card (percent attributed to assertion vs token), and an alert if rejected_assertions > 2% of proxied traffic during canary. We'll also surface top rejected_kids to catch misconfigured proxies.
Priya Nair: console UX: per-route toggle called "Accept origin assertions (beta)" with rollout slider (5/20/50/100). Toggle should show explainers: "Gateway will verify proxy-signed JWT assertions and attribute requests to asserted project when allowed." Include link to audit events.
Ethan K.: logging: reuse origin_project tag, add origin_attribution_source (assertion|token), and origin_assertion_verified boolean. Also emit audit event whenever gateway accepts an assertion where asserted proj != token proj.
Marco Li: key ops: proxies publish JWKS endpoints registered in partner truststore. Gateway caches JWKS and supports X-ASSERT-KID for rotation. We must TTL the cache and force refresh on key errors.
Julia Chen: telemetry ingestion note: keep project_id hashed in public dashboards to avoid accidental leakage. For internal dashboards we keep raw ids. Sampling: capture full trace for rejected assertions to debug.
Priya Nair: rollout plan: 1) partner proxies add assertion behind feature flag. 2) gateway code behind per-route canary toggle, default off. 3) telemetry dashboard + alert live before canary. 4) run 10% traffic for 48h, compare billing attribution.
Ethan K.: security: gateway still must check allowlist mapping proxy->allowed projects; valid signature alone is insufficient. Also rate-limit assertion acceptance per source to avoid abuse.
